lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
Date of birth: 21 Jul 1998 | Nationality: Indian
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator that tightens the previous bound by a log factor; it is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability and writes the problem sets, earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Pioneered a data-driven, research-first approach to volatility modeling that delivered robust, actionable insights.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch
Methods: time-series econometrics, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Display the code profile as a complete, usable URL.
items.because: Readers need a link they can use.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality for U.S. applications.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary and can introduce bias.

items.says: Consider adding a research area or dissertation focus.
items.because: It could support the target quant-research roles.

items.says: Define “risk-adjusted returns” and the comparison baseline.
items.because: The 35% outcome is hard to interpret and may overlap with the Sharpe claims.

items.says: Specify the evaluation period and whether the 35% figure is after costs.
items.because: The outcome is hard to interpret as written.

items.says: Qualify the claim that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: Purged splits and an embargo alone do not eliminate every source of leakage.

items.says: Specify the actual validation safeguards.
items.because: The current wording does not establish how other sources of leakage were addressed.

items.says: Clarify your contribution and relevant tools or design choices.
items.because: Those details would make the feature-store work more useful for the role.

items.says: Make sure “feature store” accurately describes what you built.
Distinguish approval of a future allocation from actual deployment and results.
items.because: Approval for the next quarter does not establish live performance.

items.says: Do not report the best of 400 backtested configurations as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the best backtest creates substantial selection bias and is not a defensible live estimate.

items.says: Resolve its apparent duplication of the Kaggle order-book result.
items.because: Both bullets claim a 0.4 Sharpe gain over 18 months out of sample.

items.says: Identify the baseline, book, evaluation period, and whether the Sharpe figure is annualized.
items.because: The comparison needs to be interpretable.

items.says: Verify that the 18-month period was genuinely out of sample.
Check and accurately describe the shared-seed setup.
items.because: Identical seeds across workers may produce duplicate or correlated runs rather than independent Monte Carlo samples.

items.says: Clarify what the timing comparison includes.
items.because: Setup or hardware may differ.

items.says: Give more context for what the variance bound improves on.
items.because: Readers need enough context to understand the theoretical contribution.

items.says: Emphasize your contribution and the paper’s review status instead of its section number.
items.because: Saying the result is “Section 3” is less useful.

items.says: Fix the tense inconsistency between “taught” and “writes.”
Clarify the teaching rating’s source and sample size if available.
items.because: Otherwise, the rating may be difficult to assess.

items.says: Add the package name or a link if available.
Identify the source of the download count.
items.because: Readers need context to interpret the total.

items.says: Replace or remove the vague, promotional bullet.
items.because: It gives no specific method or result and takes space away from evidence of the work.

items.says: Clarify the forecast measure or comparison assessed by the tests.
Explain what “both crisis periods” refers to.
Make clear whether the 24-index count applies before or after the Holm correction.
items.because: The claim could be ambiguous.

items.says: De-emphasize the working paper’s page count.
items.because: The page count is unlikely to help.

items.says: Clarify the paper’s status and whether you presented it at the seminar.
items.because: Your role in the presentation should be clear.

items.says: Provide a link to the paper if available.
Add a concrete competition outcome or remove this general bullet.
items.because: It is too general on its own, and the other bullets may already cover the contribution.

items.says: Explain what the 0.02 gap measures.
Explain why the fold change demonstrates reduced leakage rather than only changed validation behavior.
Avoid treating the leaderboard score as a clean test result.
items.because: Repeated submissions can lead to adaptation to the leaderboard.

items.says: Resolve its apparent duplication of the Northpeak order-book result.
items.because: If it is the same signal or result, it should not be claimed as a separate project outcome.

items.says: If this is distinct work, distinguish it and give enough context to evaluate the result.
items.because: The Northpeak bullet reports the same Sharpe gain and out-of-sample period.

items.says: Move PyTorch out of the programming-language category.
items.because: PyTorch is a framework, not a programming language.

items.says: Make the broad methods list more specific where substantiated.
Consider adding important technical tools used in the experience and projects to the skills section.
items.because: They may matter for the target roles but are missing there.
